claims.text: The Hofgarten is an Italian Renaissance-style garden located at the northern edge of Munich's Old Town, situated between the Residenz and the Englischer Garten.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The garden was created starting in 1613 under Duke Maximilian I of Bavaria as a northern extension of the Munich Residenz.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: At the center of the garden stands the Dianatempel, an eight-arched pavilion built in 1615 by Heinrich Schön the Elder.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The roof of the Dianatempel is crowned by a 1623 bronze replica of the Tellus Bavaria statue, created by Hubert Gerhard.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Inside the Dianatempel are four shell-decorated wall fountains that were famously mentioned in André Gide's book 'The Fruits of the Earth'.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The main western entrance, the Hofgartentor, was built in 1816 and was the first architectural work completed in Munich by Leo von Klenze.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The northern and western edges of the garden are bordered by arcades, and the western arcades feature frescoes by Peter von Cornelius depicting the history of the House of Wittelsbach.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The east side of the garden is closed by the Bavarian State Chancellery, whose central dome is a surviving relic of the former Bavarian Army Museum that was largely destroyed in World War II.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: In front of the State Chancellery stands a war memorial built in the 1920s to commemorate the people of Munich who died in the First World War.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: A black granite memorial in the northeast corner of the garden honors the White Rose group, whose members were executed for their nonviolent resistance against Hitler's regime.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The garden was heavily damaged during World War II and its reconstruction combined the original 17th-century formal Renaissance design with elements of a 19th-century landscape garden.
claims.subject: self
